verdict.rationale: Kling documents Image to Video as a priced first-party mode, including start/end-frame control and audio variants [kling-docs-20, kling-docs-21]. Its MVL framework accepts images as an input modality [kling-docs-16], and it generates product videos from product and model images [kling-docs-9]. Subject preservation is supported indirectly by the Elements persistent-identity system [kling-docs-13] and by start/end-frame anchoring, but neither is documented specifically as image-to-video fidelity. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that subject and composition are preserved from the source image, and independent or hands-on corroboration of image-to-video fidelity.
